The Verrazzano-Narrows Bridge spans the Narrows between Staten Island and Brooklyn in New York City.
Construction began in 1959 and the bridge opened to traffic on November 21, 1964. At the time of its
opening it was the longest suspension bridge main span in the world, at 4,260 feet. The bridge was named
for Giovanni da Verrazzano, an Italian explorer who in 1524 became the first European to enter New York
Harbor. The bridge deck sits 220 feet above high water at mid-span, allowing large ocean-going vessels to
pass beneath. The total length of the bridge including approaches is 9,820 feet, and the towers rise
693 feet above the water. Annual traffic exceeds 200,000 vehicles in each direction. The bridge
underwent a major rehabilitation between 2013 and 2022 that replaced all of the suspender cables and
rebuilt the deck. Engineers discovered during that work that corrosion in the anchorage housings had
proceeded further than earlier surveys had indicated, which extended the schedule by several years.
